[[Lamontville Golden Arrows F.C.|Golden Arrows]] (Coastal) | promoted = [[Ria Stars F.C.|Ria Stars]], [[Lamontville Golden Arrows F.C.|Golden Arrows]] | relegated = | matches = | total goals = | prevseason = [[1998–99 National First Division|1998–99]] | nextseason = [[2000–01 National First Division|2000–01]] }} The '''1999–2000 National First Division''' was the 4th season of [[National First Division|the second tier]] of South African [[Association football|soccer]] since the reorganisation in 1996. It consisted of two streams, an Inland stream of 16 teams, and a Coastal stream of 14 teams.{{Cite web |title=South Africa 1999/2000 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesz/zaf00.html |access-date=2023-09-01 |website=www.rsssf.org}} The Coastal stream was won by [[Lamontville Golden Arrows F.C.|Golden Arrows]], the third consecutive team from Durban to do so,https://www.iol.co.za/capeargus/sport/durban-rules-as-abaqulusi-win-first-division-511812{{Cite web |date=2023-03-20 |title=Golden Arrows |url=https://www.livesoccerscore.co.za/club/golden-arrows/ |access-date=2023-09-01 |website=Live Soccer Score South Africa |language=en-US}} and the Inland stream by [[Ria Stars F.C.|Ria Stars]], with both earning promotion to the [[2000–01 Premier Soccer League]].{{Cite web |date=2000-04-29 |title=ARROWS PROMOTED TO PREMIER LEAGUE |url=https://mg.co.za/article/2000-04-29-arrows-promoted-to-premier-league/ |access-date=2023-09-01 |website=The Mail & Guardian |language=en-ZA}} Two high-profile clubs were relegated, with [[Bush Bucks F.C.|Durban Bush Bucks]], winners of the inaugural [[1985 NSL First Division]], finishing bottom of the Coastal Stream, and [[Vaal Professionals F.C.|Vaal Professionals]], members of the inaugural [[1971 NPSL First Division|1971 Castle League]], finishing bottom of the Inland Stream.{{Cite web |title=Premier Soccer League -
